add.text: A coat hangs over the back of the chair. You don't own this coat.
A hollow in the duvet, the shape of someone lying there. You haven't lain down today.
The light under the door is broken in the middle. As if someone is standing outside.
Down on the street, someone stands with their head tilted back, looking at your window.
In the gap between the two screens, a little seawater is seeping out.
A few scales on the duvet. Silver-grey.
Water has seeped in under the door, with a ring of salt at its edge.
A crust of salt has formed on the glass.
A metal cylinder on the desk, wired up to the computer.
A letter by the pillow, in your handwriting. It doesn't read like you.
Something with wings stands outside the door. Like a fungus. Like a shrimp.
Something in the sky, flying in from a very distant star.
The picture on the screen has a photograph pinned to its back.
A painting on the wall by the bed. It shows you, lying in bed.
A hand reaches in under the door. Long nails. As if looking for food.
The takeaway on the little table has been gnawed. The teeth marks aren't human.
A circle drawn on the floor. The chair sits exactly inside it.
The creases in the sheet line up into a triangle.
A sigil drawn on the door, every stroke in the proper order.
Rain runs down the glass in streaks. Count them: seventy-two.
Thirteen pairs of chopsticks on the desk. Not one pair unwrapped.
A face pressed to the tall window, wearing a crown, backlit.
The shadow of a camel outside the door. Someone is blowing a horn.
The sun is setting in the wrong direction. It goes down on the other side of the window.
Someone is sitting in the chair. In the photo they're only an outline, like a triangle.
On the wall above the bed, the shadow of nine squares. Count them: ten.
The door is open a crack. Outside is the meeting grid.
A yellow mark on the glass. It isn't any letter.
The lamp is yellow. In the photo, everything is yellow.
Someone lies under the duvet, wearing a pale mask.
A page of the play is stuck to the door. Act Two.
Two suns outside, sinking into a lake. There is no lake outside.
A pair of scales on the desk. Wheat on one side, nothing on the other, and it hangs level.
The shadow of a black horse sits at the foot of the bed.
A bowl of barley rice by the door, still steaming.
Only one bowl left on the little table, and it's empty.
Both screens lit. A group message at three in the morning: 'Noted.'
A white marble bust lies on the bed. The face is yours.
It's very bright outside the door, as if a star fell into the stairwell from the north-east.
The curtains are drawn. You didn't draw them.
A very thick book lies open on the desk at page 751.
The tall window has become a door. It's open.
The door is two doors. One is the key, the other the guardian.
Outside, the calendar has stopped at November 1st.
The computer's power light is an eye.
Under the bed, crowded tight: tiny black hooves.
A queue outside the door, no end in sight. Everyone holds a staff badge with a blank name.
The forest outside has grown right up to the building.
The meeting on screen: twelve tiles, every one of them looking into the camera.
Scorch marks on the bed where sparks have jumped.
A tall figure in a long robe outside the door. The face is unclear, as if from very far away.
Outside, people walk in a line towards where there is no light.
Everything on the desk floats, one finger's width above it.
The bed is shaking, as if a heavy drum were beating under the floor.
The door is knocking. The photo caught the shape of the sound.
Nothing outside the window. Not black. Nothing.
You, in the chair, have turned round and are looking at the camera.
The bed is perfectly made, as if no one has slept in it. No one has, for seventeen days.
The door is open. Outside stands everyone you know, all with the same face.
The glass is covered in words: Reply to me.
A huge black dog crouches by the desk. Wet fur, many eyes. It's looking at you.
It lies across the bed, filling all of it, tentacles hanging from its jaw to the floor.
The whole door wall is its shadow.
There is no sky outside. It's one of its eyes.
